topic: Obstructions to unrestricted, reduced and full-cell surjectivity of pseudo-Frobenius row deletion
title: Extensions of Ma–Zhang's negative answer to Delgado, Süer and Yeşil's symmetrization question

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We extend Ma and Zhang's negative answer (2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24391331, Section 2) to the surjectivity question in Delgado, Süer and Yeşil, A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups (arXiv:2611.14268v1, Section 5, p. 9, final paragraph): the row-deletion map omits not only targets containing 1, but also some reduced symmetric targets whose diagrams have no full cell below the diagonal. The ordered output elements satisfy b_i >= 2i; equality at b_1 = 2 forces every element below the conductor to be even. The smallest excluded reduced target has Frobenius number 7; under the full-cell restriction the minimum is 9. We give infinite excluded families, retain the exact ordinary fiber and fixed-point characterization, and distinguish fixed-source image bounds from fixed-target counts.
summary: Every proper numerical-semigroup row-deletion output omits 1. For almost symmetric sources, output elements satisfy b_i >= 2i, and targets containing 2 are attained precisely when their elements below the conductor are all even. The minimal excluded reduced symmetric target has Frobenius 7; imposing the full-cell condition raises that minimum to 9 but does not restore surjectivity. Written proofs include both infinite excluded families, the binomial exclusion bound, the exact ordinary fiber, symmetric-semigroup fixed points and the fixed-source image bound. Prior target counting, diagram facts and examples are attributed to their sources. Exact finite checks retain their specified source and target ranges.
